top.title: 'We play with no fear!' - Mario Hermoso reveals Gian Piero Gasperini's training ground secret after AS Roma halt Paris Saint-Germain's winning streak
top.description: FBL-EUR-C1-PSG-ROMA - AFP Mario Hermoso scored early and earned Player of the Match honours as AS Roma ended Paris Saint-Germain's 100 per cent Champions League start with a 2-2 draw at the Parc des Princes. Speaking afterwards, the Spanish defender explained how Gian Piero Gasperini's fearless system empowers centre-backs to attack. Hermoso inspires fearless Roma to historic Paris point Mario Hermoso set the tone inside five minutes as AS Roma held reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain to a thrilling 2-2 draw in the first-ever meeting between the clubs on Wednesday night. Winning possession high up the pitch before finishing from Matias Soule's cut-back, the Spanish centre-back helped Gian Piero Gasperini's side end PSG's 100 per cent Champions League start despite goals from Illia Zabarnyi and Ousmane Dembele, with substitute Donyell Malen converting a late penalty after Vitinha's handball. "Everyone knows what the coach does, this is his identity, his style of playing," Hermoso told Sky Sport Italia after collecting UEFA's Player of the Match award. "We defenders get the opportunity to be protagonists, so I am very happy to come to a stadium like this, and see Roma playing in this special way, with no fear. We are on the right track and must keep taking these big steps forward." Training ground drills and Gasperini's squad rotation Gasperini sprang a tactical surprise by leaving Malen, Paulo Dybala and Bryan Cristante on the bench from the start, yet Roma's rotated line-up matched the French giants across 90 minutes. Hermoso, who also went close to adding a second open-play goal, revealed how attacking rotations are rehearsed daily. "With these team-mates who play in attack, we do try to make these moves in training sessions, everyone gets to have a go, and that means us defenders can bring something extra to the team, it's an added benefit," he explained. Addressing the bench impact, Hermoso added: "Everyone in this squad is important, we are set out in a way that we can all be protagonists. Dony, Paulo and Bryan had more minutes in this season, but they came on with the right mentality, and were ready to help get a good result." Building a winning mentality against European champions PSG only breached Roma's open-play organisation through Zabarnyi's 31st-minute corner header and Dembele's 62nd-minute spot-kick after Achraf Hakimi was fouled by Wesley. Hermoso credited Gasperini with transforming Roma's resilience in high-pressure European fixtures. "The coach gives you confidence to believe, to have this mentality of reacting to difficult moments that we suffered not just this season, but over the years," Hermoso told Prime Video . "This is important, given the way the team came in, the way we played this match against a team that has won the last two Champions Leagues. The result is a huge achievement... top.title: How OBJ stopped Gaddafi’s AK-47 convoy at Abuja airport in 2006 – Fani-Kayode
top.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini, Ambassador Olufemi Fani-Kayode, has disclosed how former President Olusegun Obasanjo refused to let assassinated Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi’s delegation bring high-powered weapons into Abuja in 2006, a decision he said saved lives. Fani-Kayode, a former minister of aviation, gave the account in a Facebook post titled “20 Years Ago With Muammar Ghaddafi!” who had then arrived in Nigeria for the African and South American Heads of State Summit. He said he received the Libyan leader at the airport on Obasanjo’s behalf and was detailed to accompany him for four days. “He arrived at the airport with no less than approximately 200 bodyguards, all with sidearms, and at least 100 cars (which had been sent ahead and were parked at the airport) to convey him to Abuja. The boot of each of those cars was filled with AK-47s and all manner of sophisticated weapons,” he said. Fani-Kayode said the convoy was blocked at the gate by Nigerian security personnel and the military. He said Gaddafi, members of his delegation and even his bodyguards would be allowed in with their sidearms, but not the weapons in the boots of the vehicles. After three more failed attempts to leave, he said, the Libyan leader lost his temper. “Ghaddafi totally lost his temper, got out of his car and started walking under the burning sun, past the airport gate and towards Abuja saying that if the cars were not allowed in he would walk there instead. Every single one of his 200 bodyguards and delegation members walked behind him!” he said. He said he called Obasanjo, who was on his way to the airport to travel to Lagos, and told Gaddafi the President was coming to settle the matter himself. Gaddafi agreed to return to the airport. Fani-Kayode said Obasanjo greeted Gaddafi warmly, apologised for the blockage and promised that the gates would be opened. But as he left, the then President whispered an instruction to him. “As he walked past me he bent over and whispered into my ear that under no circumstances would Ghaddafi and his team be allowed in unless they complied with our request that they drop the AK 47’s from the boots of their cars and put them back on their plane,” he said. He said Gaddafi’s Minister of National Security and Head of Protocol had threatened to fly the Libyan leader home and boycott the entire conference if the weapons were not allowed in. The Libyan officials complied after what he described as a “hot encounter and harsh trading of words”. top.title: Musk To Give Two SpaceX Shares To ‘Every Child In America’
top.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said Wednesday he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month. “Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally,” Musk said in a post on X, the social media platform he also owns. The world’s richest person said the share from SpaceX would be transferred next month, while the share from him personally would be transferred in June next year. He did not provide any further details about how the scheme would work. APRIL 30: Elon Musk arrives to court at the Ronald V. Dellums Federal Building on April 30, 2026 in Oakland, California. (Photo by Benjamin Fanjoy / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Benjamin Fanjoy / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP “I recommend holding on to your shares,” Musk said, claiming that SpaceX could “be worth about a million times the current global economy” if it “succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun’s energy.” “These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them,” he said. In October, Musk promised that every child in the US would receive one SpaceX share, adding that it would be “the first of many.” There are around 73 million people under the age of 18 in the country, according to 2024 data from the Census Bureau. The closing price of one SpaceX share was $127.44 on Wednesday, meaning Musk’s gift would be worth a combined $18.6 billion. SpaceX made its stock market debut in June, raising about $85.7 billion. The company’s Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the spacecraft central to Musk’s ambition to colonize Mars. top.title: Major MLS playoff overhaul confirmed as league axes wild card round and best-of-three series
top.description: Inter Miami CF v D.C. United - Getty Images Sport Major League Soccer (MLS) is finalising another major overhaul of its post-season format, with the wild card round and best-of-three first round set to be scrapped from the 2027-28 campaign. The revamped 16-team structure aims to boost regular-season intensity after the current format proved ineffective at sustaining momentum and rewarding the league's top performers. MLS set for major play-off overhaul MLS is finalising another major overhaul of its post-season structure , even as the 2026 MLS Cup play-offs get under way. Beginning with the 2027-28 season, the league will eliminate its short-lived wild card round and scrap the best-of-three first-round format, according to reports from The Guardian . The changes will condense the play-off field to 16 teams. Under the new model, the opening two rounds will be played as two-legged, home-and-away ties, while the semi-finals and final will revert to single-elimination matches hosted by the higher seed. Why the league is scrapping best-of-three Introduced in 2023, the best-of-three opening round has proved ineffective at sustaining drama or rewarding regular-season excellence. Over the past three campaigns, a staggering 35 days elapsed between the end of the regular season and the second round due to the November international break. While the 2026 World Cup break allowed MLS to push the start of this year's play-offs past the international window, the gap from Decision Day to the quarter-finals still stretched to 28 days. The league had also weighed an Australian rules football-inspired double-elimination model before settling on its latest plan. Although an MLS spokesperson did not immediately comment on the latest reports, the league confirmed its review back in August. "Major League Soccer is continuing to evaluate potential adjustments to its postseason format as part of a broader review of the league’s shift to a new competition calendar, beginning with the 2027-28 season," a spokesperson said at the time. A bid to restore regular-season intensity A primary driver behind the constant adjustments is the desire to raise the stakes of the regular season. Currently, 60 per cent of clubs qualify for the play-offs, creating an overly forgiving race. That leniency was highlighted this year when Real Salt Lake reached the first round despite winning just once in 16 matches after the World Cup. They edged out Minnesota United on Decision Day, even though Minnesota had endured a run of one victory in 18 games. The 2027-28 model will become the sixth different play-off format MLS has used since its 1996 launch. The league briefly abandoned multi-legged ties in 2019 before reintroducing extended series following its broadcast partnership with Apple, partly to guarantee lower-ranked qualifiers at least one match of post-season revenue. top.title: Exeter not 'the finished article', says boss Taylor
top.description: Matt Taylor has seen his side lose just one of their past 10 games in all competitions - away at League Two leaders Salford City [Shutterstock] Exeter City are "nowhere near the finished article" despite their recent upturn in form, manager Matt Taylor has said. Having been a point above the relegation places at the end of September, Exeter have become one of League Two's in-form teams. They have lost just one of their past 10 matches in all competitions, keeping clean sheets in half of those games. It has seen them rise to eighth in the division and also book an FA Cup second round tie after winning at then League One leaders Huddersfield Town in the first round. "The last 10 games now has been a period of games where we lost one, and that was as good a performance as we've had all season at Salford against a very strong opposition, incredible cup results and good league form," Taylor told BBC Radio Devon. "So we're going in the right direction, but nowhere near the finished article. "We'll constantly have challenges in-game and in the lead-up to games with the way we are as a group in terms of real depth and experience. "But in terms of the strides and the progress I think individuals have made within the team in that period I'm speaking about, I think you can see players are performing to a better level and with a bigger output and a bigger influence on the game. "I've always said I'll sleep well at night as long as the group is honest with me. "I feel this is a really honest group, but I'm still as excited as ever to see where it could take us in two weeks' time, in two months' time, in two years' time for some of them, but certainly as this season goes deeper seeing where we're at." Exeter defender Harper 'honoured' by Kenya cap Taylor impressed with Exeter City's Oldham comeback Exeter host a resurgent Crawley Town on Saturday (12:30 GMT) with the joint-second best home record in League Two. They have conceded just twice in eight games at St James Park, winning five and drawing the other three. It is a record that Taylor is proud of, having won their past four home games. "There's certain records we're really proud of this season: our defensive record, clean sheets, our home record, our home form," added Taylor. "Even more so because it connects the team with the fans. You want a strong home showing. "Very rarely this season do I think our home fans have gone home disappointed or frustrated with what they've seen and that's the majority of our fan base, that's where they get to see us, close to home, less travel involved. "Also, we have to take into account how far opposition teams have to travel down to us, same for us when we go to Oldham and Crawley, all these teams away from home, not just the north but London-based as well. top.title: 19 Hillsdale County volleyball athletes earn all-league SCAA-East
top.description: ILLSDALE COUNTY — Hillsdale County volleyball programs dominated the Southern Central Athletic Association East Division postseason honors following the 2026 fall sports season, accounting for all four Dream Team selections and 19 all-conference honorees. Hillsdale Academy seniors Lucy Cote and Malorie-Kate Apel and Pittsford juniors Alexis Bryner and Karmin Butler earned SCAA Dream Team honors, while Pittsford head coach Jessica Butler was named the division’s coach of the year. Butler led the Wildcats to a 21-12 overall record, their best finish since 2022, and an appearance in the Division 4 district championship game. Bryner, Cote and Apel also earned all-region honors from the Michigan Interscholastic Volleyball Coaches Association this fall. Hillsdale Academy earned six all-conference selections after finishing the season 23-9 and capturing its fourth consecutive district championship along with the division crown. Joining Cote and Apel with first-team honors was fellow senior Zoe Plemmons. Camden-Frontier junior Zailey Conroy rounded out Hillsdale County’s first-team selections. Local athletes accounted for six of the seven first-team honorees. Five more Hillsdale County athletes earned second-team honors, including Pittsford freshman Layla Bryner and sophomore Ellie Bump, Hillsdale Academy junior Abigail Kriesch and freshman Lucy Molenkamp and Camden-Frontier junior Alyssa Schroeder. Litchfield, Waldron and North Adams-Jerome were also represented among the honorable mention selections, with all six Hillsdale County programs competing in the division earning postseason recognition. The young defender came in as a 64th minute replacement for Frenkie de Jong and had a solid enough outing. An answer to Barcelona’s defensive problems? Alex Campos made his debut against Sabah. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) It is no secret that Barcelona are struggling defensively. Even Hansi Flick looked visibly frustrated after the team conceded a goal against Sabah. The team simply lacks enough depth in central defence. But as reported by Diario SPORT , Flick may have found his answer in the form of Campos. With Andreas Christensen still struggling with injuries, Pau Cubarsi carrying a knock and the likes of Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde often required elsewhere, Barcelona have been crying out for a reliable centre-back. De Jong has done well to chip in, but he is not a natural in this position, leaving Flick with Gerard Martin as the only other option. Campos’ cameo in Baku may prove to be a first step towards him becoming a real alternative for Barcelona. The report frames the youngster as a potential example of Barcleona solving the defensive problem from within. The Catalans have a solid track record of doing so, having previously solved multiple problems for giving chances to academy players such as Marc Casado, Marc Bernal, Fermin Lopez and Cubarsi himself. What does Campos bring to the table? Campos is rated highly by Bojan. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) As far as his profile is concerned, Campos is quite similar to Cubarsi. Originally a midfielder before Barcelona converted him into a central defender, Campos’ natural qualities include playing out from the back and the ability to join attacks. He is also a genuine threat from set-pieces and is very efficient on the ball. Under Juliano Belletti, however, his defensive game has improved enormously and he is now regarded as a solid, reliable operator in central defence. Campos is also quite versatile, as he can perform both as a left and a right sided centre-back. He is comfortable filling in as a holding midfielder as well. Perhaps more importantly, Campos rarely loses his composure. He is already held in high regard by the likes of Bojan Krkic and Belletti and it will be interesting to see if he is used more often by Flick in the coming weeks.

top.title: Jose Mourinho identifies key issue with Real Madrid’s squad players after PSV scare
top.description: Jose Mourinho identifies key issue with Real Madrid’s squad players after PSV scare Real Madrid have secured ten successive wins in all competitions and are looking like the team to beat at the moment. However, the team is not without its faults, and it was evident in the first half of their game against PSV Eindhoven in the UEFA Champions League. The defensive duo of Antonio Rudiger and Eder Militao looked completely out of sorts , prompting Jose Mourinho to make changes in the second half. Mourinho identifies a key issue Mourinho wants more quality from his second squad. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) As reported by Defensa Central , Mourinho believes that his rotation options are simply not performing as expected. The Real Madrid coach has observed that when the fringe players come in, Real Madrid often lose their brightness and competitive edge. It is a pattern that Mourinho has noticed on multiple occasions, with the likes of Rudiger, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Alvaro Carreras and Eduardo Camavinga often failing to perform to the expected level. These players have lacked the quality and the consistency the first-choice XI has provided this season, and the 5-1 win over PSV was the latest example. Mourinho made six changes to the starting lineup, but the team struggled in the first half and conceded. He had experienced similar situations in the comebacks against Celta Vigo and AEK Athens. A necessary balancing act Mourinho is using Luis Enrique’s playbook. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) Despite this shortcoming from lesser-used players, Mourinho remains committed to using the full depth of his squad. The Portuguese is working on managing a demanding schedule in December through a selection rest plan. He is determined to keep his first-choice players fresh for key matches. With Real Madrid facing a relentless run of fixtures, rotation will indeed play a key role in the month of December, and that is when Mourinho needs his second-fiddle stars to perform well. In many ways, Mourinho is applying the same roadmap used by Luis Enrique at PSG, protecting his important players in selected games. He rested Arda Guler and Tchouameni against AEK, and left Jude Bellingham on the bench against PSV Eindhoven. This is yet another indicator that Mourinho has stressed massively on ensuring the well-being of his trusted individuals. But for this formula to work, players such as Trent, Rudiger, Camavinga, and others must step up their game.

top.title: Joshua Zirkzee makes his position unmistakable after Man United’s controversy-filled Sporting encounter
top.description: Joshua Zirkzee makes his position unmistakable after Man United’s controversy-filled Sporting encounter Joshua Zirkzee has made his feelings crystal clear after Manchester United’s controversy-filled 2-2 Champions League draw against Sporting CP. Controversy Pochettino was denied his first win as United head coach, with multiple bizarre refereeing decisions going against him and his players. Referee Szymon Marciniak ruled out an Amad Diallo goal during the second half, having adjudged Youri Tielemans to have committed a foul in the build-up. Marciniak’s whistle came just before Amad found the net, ruling out any VAR intervention. The Polish referee compounded matters by awarding Sporting a debatable first-half penalty and disallowing what would have been a late United winner for a push on goalkeeper Kaique Pereira. The decision to chalk off United’s goal seemed baffling given that he allowed a similar Suárez goal to stand when there was slight contact with Senne Lammens . Pochettino hit out at the decisions in his post-match remarks to reporters , but he chose to emphasise the positives and the fine attitude his players displayed. In an interview with MUTV , Zirkzee acknowledged how costly the referee’s shocking performance had been, but insisted it was solely down to him and his teammates to deliver the victory. Zirkzee’s verdict The Dutchman told club media, “In my opinion, there were definitely some key decisions there that didn’t really favour us. We shouldn’t look at the referee, we should look at ourselves instead, but it definitely has an impact on us, you can’t deny that.” “But the team that we have, we should come here and not look at the ref and make sure that we get the win, regardless of the decisions that he makes.” He continued, “Obviously, we did come here to win, so in a way, we’ve got some positives to take.” “But with our recent form, of course, we’re disappointed to not win. Some positives to take, we’ve just got to keep moving forward, keep going together, keep putting in the work and move onto the next game.” Zirkzee said of his return to the starting XI, “I’m very happy; every game you play for this club is an honour. I’ve been here for some time and it’s been a while since I started a game, so I’m very happy, I just wish we could have got a win.” “For where we’re standing at right now, to have a fanbase like that is just incredible. All we can do is get up the next day and make sure the next time they travel with us and the next time they watch our game, we repay it, so that’s all we can do for now.” Looking ahead to Saturday’s meeting with Brentford, Zirkzee remarked, “It’s a big test. The fans deserve a result and all we want is a result. We’ve got to dig ourselves out of the trenches.” United sit in 19th place in the Premier League table heading into the game against Brentford.

top.title: AI solved the hardest problem in maths – is there anything it can’t do?
top.description: Alzheimer’s disease, involving amyloid plaques in the brain, will be tough for AI to solve JUAN GAERTNER/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY The progress AI has made in mathematics this year is nothing short of extraordinary. In January, I was impressed to see relatively minor open problems tackled with the help of AI . Now, AI is being used to solve the hardest problems in maths . The obvious next question is, if AI can do this, is there anything it can’t do? That is the inference that the AI companies want us to make, but, in reality, the answer is much more nuanced. Read more Mathematicians are amazed by ‘holy grail’ proof of Riemann hypothesis We see this messaging in claims that AI can “solve X”, where X is any field of human endeavour you care to name. Biology is a big one. “Cancer, Alzheimer’s, heart disease, mental illness – these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade,” said Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei while promoting the company’s recent initial public offering . “I think one day maybe we can cure all disease with the help of AI,” said Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind, last year , adding that this could be “within the next decade or so”. This phenomenon isn’t new: I call it “physicist brain”, after the propensity for physicists to wade into areas outside their expertise and declare simple solutions. More broadly, it is called Nobel disease , after the many Nobel prizewinners who have gone on to make, shall we say, less evidenced-backed claims. In general, there is a tendency to think that if an intelligent person is good at one thing, they are good at many other things that require intelligence. What is different now is that trillion-dollar companies and large swathes of the global economy now depend on this being true of artificial intelligence. Advertisement To be clear, I think we must now admit that AI is better at solving open mathematical problems than any human, and that this has happened faster than anyone ever expected. When I first saw the news in September that the Navier-Stokes problem had been solved by OpenAI , I felt stunned. We had entered a new world. With the announcement of the Riemann hypothesis proof this week, I felt sick and had to go and have a lie-down. These were intellectual Everests I have marvelled at since my teenage years, conquered by a machine far sooner than anyone expected. You may have read my recent piece forecasting the future in 2096 – an early draft had a line, later removed, about three Millennium Prize Problems being solved by AI in the 2030s. nigeria.title: How OBJ stopped Gaddafi’s AK-47 convoy at Abuja airport in 2006 – Fani-Kayode
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini, Ambassador Olufemi Fani-Kayode, has disclosed how former President Olusegun Obasanjo refused to let assassinated Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi’s delegation bring high-powered weapons into Abuja in 2006, a decision he said saved lives. Fani-Kayode, a former minister of aviation, gave the account in a Facebook post titled “20 Years Ago With Muammar Ghaddafi!” who had then arrived in Nigeria for the African and South American Heads of State Summit. He said he received the Libyan leader at the airport on Obasanjo’s behalf and was detailed to accompany him for four days. “He arrived at the airport with no less than approximately 200 bodyguards, all with sidearms, and at least 100 cars (which had been sent ahead and were parked at the airport) to convey him to Abuja. The boot of each of those cars was filled with AK-47s and all manner of sophisticated weapons,” he said. Fani-Kayode said the convoy was blocked at the gate by Nigerian security personnel and the military. He said Gaddafi, members of his delegation and even his bodyguards would be allowed in with their sidearms, but not the weapons in the boots of the vehicles. After three more failed attempts to leave, he said, the Libyan leader lost his temper. “Ghaddafi totally lost his temper, got out of his car and started walking under the burning sun, past the airport gate and towards Abuja saying that if the cars were not allowed in he would walk there instead. Every single one of his 200 bodyguards and delegation members walked behind him!” he said. He said he called Obasanjo, who was on his way to the airport to travel to Lagos, and told Gaddafi the President was coming to settle the matter himself. Gaddafi agreed to return to the airport. Fani-Kayode said Obasanjo greeted Gaddafi warmly, apologised for the blockage and promised that the gates would be opened. But as he left, the then President whispered an instruction to him. “As he walked past me he bent over and whispered into my ear that under no circumstances would Ghaddafi and his team be allowed in unless they complied with our request that they drop the AK 47’s from the boots of their cars and put them back on their plane,” he said. He said Gaddafi’s Minister of National Security and Head of Protocol had threatened to fly the Libyan leader home and boycott the entire conference if the weapons were not allowed in. nigeria.title: US lists 63 professions eligible for 3-year work visa
nigeria.description: The US has outlined 63 professional categories whose qualified practitioners can apply for a temporary work visa allowing them to take up employment in the country for up to three years. The arrangement, known as the Trade National (TN) visa, is available exclusively to citizens of Canada and Mexico under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). The TN visa allows eligible professionals from the two neighbouring countries to work for US employers in specified occupations, provided they meet the educational, professional and employment requirements attached to their chosen fields. According to the US Department of State, applicants must be citizens of either Canada or Mexico, have a profession recognised under the USMCA list, secure a prearranged job with a US employer and possess the qualifications required for the position. The list covers several professional sectors, including healthcare, engineering, science, education, accounting and other specialised occupations. Some of the professions recognised under the arrangement include accountants, architects, engineers, lawyers, pharmacists, registered nurses, dentists, veterinarians, economists, mathematicians, scientists, university lecturers and computer systems analysts. Other eligible occupations include agriculturalists, biologists, chemists, geologists, meteorologists, psychologists, social workers, urban planners and technical publications writers. However, appearing on the list does not automatically guarantee approval, as applicants must demonstrate that they satisfy the specific educational or professional requirements for their occupations. Most of the listed professions require a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent, although some categories permit alternative qualifications or professional credentials. The US government also requires applicants to provide details of their proposed employment, including their job responsibilities, expected duration of stay, qualifications and remuneration arrangements. Under Section 214.6 of Title 8 of the US Code of Federal Regulations, successful TN applicants can be admitted into the country for a period not exceeding three years. The classification can also be extended, subject to the applicant continuing to meet the relevant requirements. The application process differs slightly between the two eligible nationalities. Canadian citizens can generally apply for TN status at a US port of entry or designated pre-clearance facility without first obtaining a TN visa from a US embassy. Mexican citizens, however, must obtain a TN nonimmigrant visa from a US embassy or consulate before seeking admission into the country. The arrangement was originally introduced under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), which came into force in 1994. It was retained when the USMCA replaced NAFTA on July 1, 2020. El Nino is a naturally occurring weather phenomenon that emerges from the Pacific approximately every two to seven years. It shifts global rain patterns and brings higher temperatures to much of the planet, exacerbating rising temperatures caused by climate change. This year’s El Nino has already impacted maize in central America, fishery catches in Peru and sugar and rice production in Southeast Asia. nigeria.title: Trump, NATO chief urge Russia not to ‘expand’ Ukraine war
nigeria.description: US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte urged Russia not to “expand the war” in Ukraine, in a joint statement issued Wednesday after meeting in Florida. The “outstanding” and “very impactful” meeting focused on the wars in Ukraine and Iran, said the statement issued by the White House after the closed-door talks at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort. “We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible,” the statement added. The joint appeal by Trump and Rutte comes despite the US leader describing Russian President Vladimir Putin as “my friend” during a meeting in China last week. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has taken issue with Trump’s comments on Putin. “For us, he is a killer,” Zelensky told CNN. Rutte was asked about Trump’s comments in an interview with Fox News’ “Fox & Friends” on Wednesday. “What President Trump is doing, also in the meeting in Shenzhen, is testing Putin,” the NATO secretary general said. “How serious is he? Is he willing to come to the negotiating table? Is he willing to really engage in talks. “So let’s keep the pressure on. I think it is working, and we have to keep that going.” Trump, accused by critics of siding with Moscow over Kyiv, said following his meeting with Putin that the Russian leader wants to see the war end by “diplomatic means.” The Florida meeting comes as European nations have expressed a desire to join preliminary talks that have so far only included Ukraine, the United States and Russia. Rutte said any agreement is going to have to include security guarantees for Ukraine. “When the war ends, either with a peace deal, preferable, or if not possible, a long-term ceasefire, we need to make sure that Ukraine has the security guarantees going forward,” he said. “But the most important thing here,” Rutte added, “is that we have to make sure that Ukraine has what it needs to keep the fight going, being so successful and putting that maximum pressure on the Russians.” Trump and Rutte also discussed increasing defense spending, which the US president has pressed European powers to do, the joint statement said. entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). sports.title: Major MLS playoff overhaul confirmed as league axes wild card round and best-of-three series
sports.description: Inter Miami CF v D.C. United - Getty Images Sport Major League Soccer (MLS) is finalising another major overhaul of its post-season format, with the wild card round and best-of-three first round set to be scrapped from the 2027-28 campaign. The revamped 16-team structure aims to boost regular-season intensity after the current format proved ineffective at sustaining momentum and rewarding the league's top performers. MLS set for major play-off overhaul MLS is finalising another major overhaul of its post-season structure , even as the 2026 MLS Cup play-offs get under way. Beginning with the 2027-28 season, the league will eliminate its short-lived wild card round and scrap the best-of-three first-round format, according to reports from The Guardian . The changes will condense the play-off field to 16 teams. Under the new model, the opening two rounds will be played as two-legged, home-and-away ties, while the semi-finals and final will revert to single-elimination matches hosted by the higher seed. Why the league is scrapping best-of-three Introduced in 2023, the best-of-three opening round has proved ineffective at sustaining drama or rewarding regular-season excellence. Over the past three campaigns, a staggering 35 days elapsed between the end of the regular season and the second round due to the November international break. While the 2026 World Cup break allowed MLS to push the start of this year's play-offs past the international window, the gap from Decision Day to the quarter-finals still stretched to 28 days. The league had also weighed an Australian rules football-inspired double-elimination model before settling on its latest plan. Although an MLS spokesperson did not immediately comment on the latest reports, the league confirmed its review back in August. "Major League Soccer is continuing to evaluate potential adjustments to its postseason format as part of a broader review of the league’s shift to a new competition calendar, beginning with the 2027-28 season," a spokesperson said at the time. A bid to restore regular-season intensity A primary driver behind the constant adjustments is the desire to raise the stakes of the regular season. Currently, 60 per cent of clubs qualify for the play-offs, creating an overly forgiving race. That leniency was highlighted this year when Real Salt Lake reached the first round despite winning just once in 16 matches after the World Cup. They edged out Minnesota United on Decision Day, even though Minnesota had endured a run of one victory in 18 games. The 2027-28 model will become the sixth different play-off format MLS has used since its 1996 launch. The league briefly abandoned multi-legged ties in 2019 before reintroducing extended series following its broadcast partnership with Apple, partly to guarantee lower-ranked qualifiers at least one match of post-season revenue. "We'll constantly have challenges in-game and in the lead-up to games with the way we are as a group in terms of real depth and experience. sports.title: Barcelona may have found their defensive answers in La Masia starlet – report
sports.description: Barcelona may have found their defensive answers in La Masia starlet – report Barcelona extended their winning run to five matches in all competitions following a 4-1 win over Sabah in the UEFA Champions League. Apart from the stellar attacking display, a key highlight of the night was the debut of La Masia starlet Alex Campos. The young defender came in as a 64th minute replacement for Frenkie de Jong and had a solid enough outing. An answer to Barcelona’s defensive problems? Alex Campos made his debut against Sabah. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) It is no secret that Barcelona are struggling defensively. Even Hansi Flick looked visibly frustrated after the team conceded a goal against Sabah. The team simply lacks enough depth in central defence. But as reported by Diario SPORT , Flick may have found his answer in the form of Campos. With Andreas Christensen still struggling with injuries, Pau Cubarsi carrying a knock and the likes of Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde often required elsewhere, Barcelona have been crying out for a reliable centre-back. De Jong has done well to chip in, but he is not a natural in this position, leaving Flick with Gerard Martin as the only other option. Campos’ cameo in Baku may prove to be a first step towards him becoming a real alternative for Barcelona. The report frames the youngster as a potential example of Barcleona solving the defensive problem from within. The Catalans have a solid track record of doing so, having previously solved multiple problems for giving chances to academy players such as Marc Casado, Marc Bernal, Fermin Lopez and Cubarsi himself. What does Campos bring to the table? Campos is rated highly by Bojan. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) As far as his profile is concerned, Campos is quite similar to Cubarsi. Originally a midfielder before Barcelona converted him into a central defender, Campos’ natural qualities include playing out from the back and the ability to join attacks. He is also a genuine threat from set-pieces and is very efficient on the ball. Under Juliano Belletti, however, his defensive game has improved enormously and he is now regarded as a solid, reliable operator in central defence. Campos is also quite versatile, as he can perform both as a left and a right sided centre-back. He is comfortable filling in as a holding midfielder as well. Perhaps more importantly, Campos rarely loses his composure. He is already held in high regard by the likes of Bojan Krkic and Belletti and it will be interesting to see if he is used more often by Flick in the coming weeks.

sports.title: Jose Mourinho identifies key issue with Real Madrid’s squad players after PSV scare
sports.description: Jose Mourinho identifies key issue with Real Madrid’s squad players after PSV scare Real Madrid have secured ten successive wins in all competitions and are looking like the team to beat at the moment. However, the team is not without its faults, and it was evident in the first half of their game against PSV Eindhoven in the UEFA Champions League. The defensive duo of Antonio Rudiger and Eder Militao looked completely out of sorts , prompting Jose Mourinho to make changes in the second half. Mourinho identifies a key issue Mourinho wants more quality from his second squad. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) As reported by Defensa Central , Mourinho believes that his rotation options are simply not performing as expected. The Real Madrid coach has observed that when the fringe players come in, Real Madrid often lose their brightness and competitive edge. It is a pattern that Mourinho has noticed on multiple occasions, with the likes of Rudiger, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Alvaro Carreras and Eduardo Camavinga often failing to perform to the expected level. These players have lacked the quality and the consistency the first-choice XI has provided this season, and the 5-1 win over PSV was the latest example. Mourinho made six changes to the starting lineup, but the team struggled in the first half and conceded. He had experienced similar situations in the comebacks against Celta Vigo and AEK Athens. A necessary balancing act Mourinho is using Luis Enrique’s playbook. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) Despite this shortcoming from lesser-used players, Mourinho remains committed to using the full depth of his squad. The Portuguese is working on managing a demanding schedule in December through a selection rest plan. He is determined to keep his first-choice players fresh for key matches. With Real Madrid facing a relentless run of fixtures, rotation will indeed play a key role in the month of December, and that is when Mourinho needs his second-fiddle stars to perform well. In many ways, Mourinho is applying the same roadmap used by Luis Enrique at PSG, protecting his important players in selected games. He rested Arda Guler and Tchouameni against AEK, and left Jude Bellingham on the bench against PSV Eindhoven. This is yet another indicator that Mourinho has stressed massively on ensuring the well-being of his trusted individuals. But for this formula to work, players such as Trent, Rudiger, Camavinga, and others must step up their game.

sports.title: Joshua Zirkzee makes his position unmistakable after Man United’s controversy-filled Sporting encounter
sports.description: Joshua Zirkzee makes his position unmistakable after Man United’s controversy-filled Sporting encounter Joshua Zirkzee has made his feelings crystal clear after Manchester United’s controversy-filled 2-2 Champions League draw against Sporting CP. Controversy Pochettino was denied his first win as United head coach, with multiple bizarre refereeing decisions going against him and his players. Referee Szymon Marciniak ruled out an Amad Diallo goal during the second half, having adjudged Youri Tielemans to have committed a foul in the build-up. Marciniak’s whistle came just before Amad found the net, ruling out any VAR intervention. The Polish referee compounded matters by awarding Sporting a debatable first-half penalty and disallowing what would have been a late United winner for a push on goalkeeper Kaique Pereira. The decision to chalk off United’s goal seemed baffling given that he allowed a similar Suárez goal to stand when there was slight contact with Senne Lammens . Pochettino hit out at the decisions in his post-match remarks to reporters , but he chose to emphasise the positives and the fine attitude his players displayed. In an interview with MUTV , Zirkzee acknowledged how costly the referee’s shocking performance had been, but insisted it was solely down to him and his teammates to deliver the victory. Zirkzee’s verdict The Dutchman told club media, “In my opinion, there were definitely some key decisions there that didn’t really favour us. We shouldn’t look at the referee, we should look at ourselves instead, but it definitely has an impact on us, you can’t deny that.” “But the team that we have, we should come here and not look at the ref and make sure that we get the win, regardless of the decisions that he makes.” He continued, “Obviously, we did come here to win, so in a way, we’ve got some positives to take.” “But with our recent form, of course, we’re disappointed to not win. Some positives to take, we’ve just got to keep moving forward, keep going together, keep putting in the work and move onto the next game.” Zirkzee said of his return to the starting XI, “I’m very happy; every game you play for this club is an honour. I’ve been here for some time and it’s been a while since I started a game, so I’m very happy, I just wish we could have got a win.” “For where we’re standing at right now, to have a fanbase like that is just incredible. All we can do is get up the next day and make sure the next time they travel with us and the next time they watch our game, we repay it, so that’s all we can do for now.” Looking ahead to Saturday’s meeting with Brentford, Zirkzee remarked, “It’s a big test. The fans deserve a result and all we want is a result. We’ve got to dig ourselves out of the trenches.” United sit in 19th place in the Premier League table heading into the game against Brentford.

Modi suggested that parents of three-year-old children should enter data about their offspring’s activities and accomplishments into a government-run system that is also accessible to teachers and even a child’s friends. Those records, the PM suggested, will “help identify children's interests and aptitude from an early age and redirect them in the study of their choice in future.” That’s not an entirely creepy idea, because gaining access to India’s top tertiary institutions requires students to pay a hefty fee to sit for entrance exams. Modi pitched recommendations from the AI-powered app as something parents will appreciate as they contemplate whether to fund their offspring’s studies. India’s most populous state, Uttar Pradesh (UP), has proposed to build an “AI Stack” to serve its 240 million-plus residents. A 178-page tender seeks bidders to build a system that uses the state’s Family ID – a unique identifier for each household – to link data held by multiple agencies so it can be put to work in a dozen AI use cases. One of those use cases is a tool for “AI-Enabled Social Media Monitoring and Urban Grievance Detection” that “analyses publicly available social media content including online news channels and connected grievance channels to detect emerging urban issues, citizen complaints, service interruptions, and recurring service gaps.” The government wants that system to autonomously route complaints to relevant agencies, to automate actions like sending crews to patch up damaged roads. Critics have pointed to vague wording in the tender as potentially allowing the UP government to link this system to other agencies – a matter of concern given Indian state and national governments have implemented internet shutdowns to stop protestors from communicating on social media services and messaging apps. Another use case is a knowledge assistant for state police that looks up case histories and other data but can’t use it to assess evidence or provide investigative conclusions. An app for teachers will advise them on how to create custom content to meet students’ needs. Healthcare workers would also get an app to help them make recommendations during patient visits. Citizens get natural language interfaces to a system that offers advice on how to identify and access government services and schemes. UP wants to drive these apps with self-hosted open-weight models, and to use only anonymized datasets. technology.title: The sky was once full of stars, kids; then the FCC let Elon Musk launch a million datacenter satellites
technology.description: The United States Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to launch a million datacenter satellites. The regulator on Wednesday published an order [PDF] allowing SpaceX to operate a “Non-geostationary satellite orbit (NGSO) constellation of 1,000,000 satellites deployed into orbital shells each spanning 50 km at altitudes from 500 to 1,002 km and in 30-degree inclinations and sun-synchronous inclinations.” The order requires SpaceX to ensure its satellites’ radios don’t interfere with US government systems which use the 28.6-29.1 GHz band and requires the company to stick to operating within the parameters it files with the International Telecommunications Union. SpaceX asked the FCC to waive its rule requiring the atmospheric disposal of dead satellites orbiting at 2,000 km or less. Elon Musk’s company asked for “flexibility to dispose satellites operating above 600 km altitude into Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” The FCC found SpaceX did not provide enough information to let it assess if proposed “alternative disposal methods” are compliant with regulations, so deferred its decision on the waiver request. “SpaceX must file an application for modification of this authorization and provide sufficient justification for any requested waiver(s) of the Commission’s rules,” the order states. The company must also file twice-yearly reports about “conjunction events” – moments when its satellites get dangerously close to each other, or other orbiters. Whether orbiting datacenters are feasible, make sense, or will ever pay for themselves, remain open questions. Analyst firm Gartner has described the idea as “ peak insanity .” Google thinks orbiting datacenters become viable if launch costs fall to $200/kg, which would mean SpaceX needs to launch its massive Starship 1,800 times. SpaceX’s assumptions assume near-daily launches, far better than its current cadence of a launch every three days or so. Fundamental networking research must also come to fruition to handle the amount of traffic large constellations of orbiting datacenters will create. Terrestrial manufacturing capacity will also need to increase to build all those satellites. Elon Musk’s companies and Intel have planned a giant new fab to make that possible, without explaining how the supply chains behind chip manufacturing will scale to make it feasible. That's a notable omission given that semiconductor supply chains are already extremely strained. Approval for SpaceX is therefore nice but in no way a roadmap to a million datacenter satellites. Google, ironically, is a little further along than SpaceX, having launched a test sat in October and last week announcing it has hired Amazon founder Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin to launch a larger satellite carrying the equivalent of a full datacenter rack in early 2029. technology.title: European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment
technology.description: Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory. Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid's 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation. But scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next. Read full article Comments

technology.title: The security of US water systems is even leakier than we thought
technology.description: American water systems are even less secure than we thought, according to a study of 236 technology vendors that provide gear to US drinking water, wastewater, and industrial water systems. The federal government has issued 4,014 security advisories for industrial control systems and cataloged 1,792 vulnerabilities known to have been exploited in cyberattacks. A new index, called Water Supply Chain Watch and published by exposure management firm Securin, however, found almost twice as many vulnerabilities as public records identified – including 20 exploited flaws that weren't even in the federal government's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The security provider compared data on water-tech vendors with records from the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the FBI, and WaterISAC, drawing on CISA advisory data through November 20 and KEV catalog entries through November 23. It found that federal water advisories hit their highest level this year since 2020. However, the volume of security alerts isn't a reliable predictor of real-world attacks, the researchers noted. Five vendors – Rockwell Automation (58), Advantech (48), Schneider Electric (35), Siemens (26), and ABB (24) – account for 191 of the 376 water-tagged security advisories. The No. 2 firm, Advantech, accounted for the highest number of vulnerabilities rated critical, but none of the CVEs in its advisories appear in CISA's KEV catalog. Unitronics, on the other hand, accounted for only two water-tagged security advisories, but at least 75 of its controllers were compromised between November 2023 and January 2024 by attackers taking advantage of default or missing passwords. The report also highlights another disconnect between water-related CVEs and real-world cyberattacks, which don't always require attackers to exploit software bugs. The July intrusions, which security researchers suspect were the work of Iran-linked attackers , targeted more than 100 water systems , with incidents reported across at least 12 states , and involved poorly secured internet-connected controllers . According to Securin, 791 Rockwell MicroLogix 1400 controllers across multiple industries in the US were exposed to the internet as of November 17. Additionally, research by Forescout cited by the security shop found that most exposed Rockwell controllers in the US – seven in 10 – sit on mobile carrier networks, where poorly secured cellular modems can provide an entry point for attackers. technology.title: Huawei and crew tout homegrown EDA tools to overcome China’s fab deficit
technology.description: Chinese telecom and IT giant Huawei boasted about its advancements in domestic electronic design automation (EDA) software this week, which it needs to accelerate the adoption of homegrown chip manufacturing. EDA is an umbrella term for software, hardware, and services essential to the planning, design, and production of modern chips. Today, Cadence Design Systems, Synopsys, and Siemens dominate the industry, but US export controls have restricted Huawei and other blacklisted Chinese businesses' access to their tools. The US blacklisted Huawei back in 2019 over concerns the telecommunications equipment giant could be forced to inject backdoors into its gear. Unable to access top EDA tools, Huawei’s chip division, HiSilicon, was forced to develop its own with the help of Phlexing Technology. This week, Phlexing chairman Qing He detailed the company’s efforts to bring new EDA tools to support Huawei’s so-called Tau Scaling Law design philosophy. “Tau EDA is the domestic EDA tool chain for Tau chips. It comes from a long, close partnership with Huawei,” he said. We discussed the tech earlier this year, but in a nutshell, it involves using advanced packaging, specifically 3D hybrid bonding, to achieve higher transistor density for a given area. The TSMC of China, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), is still years behind Taiwan, South Korea, and the US on process technology. It currently has the ability to mass-produce chips on the equivalent of a 7 nm process. For comparison, TSMC began producing 5 nm-class products in 2020 and commenced mass production of 2 nm-class chips in late 2025. So, Huawei aims to use 3D packaging to close the gap, but for this to happen, it first needs tools capable of designing such chips, and that’s just what Phlexing claims to have done with its GloryBolt and GloryEX platforms. “Traditional EDA has long handled only single processes. Tau EDA needs to integrate and decompose multiple processes,” He said. “Coupling multi-scale, multi-structure, and multi-physics issues called for new analysis tools.” This, He says, culminated in the co-development of a process design kit (PDK) with Huawei beginning in 2024. These technologies have now gone live. The development comes as Huawei looks to bring larger, more capable processors to market. We previously discussed the company’s latest developments around AI accelerators, near packaged optics, networking, and rack systems. Many of these advancements will depend on multi-die chip packages, enabled by EDA tools, like those built by Phlexing. ®

science.title: AI solved the hardest problem in maths – is there anything it can’t do?
science.description: Alzheimer’s disease, involving amyloid plaques in the brain, will be tough for AI to solve JUAN GAERTNER/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY The progress AI has made in mathematics this year is nothing short of extraordinary. In January, I was impressed to see relatively minor open problems tackled with the help of AI . Now, AI is being used to solve the hardest problems in maths . The obvious next question is, if AI can do this, is there anything it can’t do? That is the inference that the AI companies want us to make, but, in reality, the answer is much more nuanced. Read more Mathematicians are amazed by ‘holy grail’ proof of Riemann hypothesis We see this messaging in claims that AI can “solve X”, where X is any field of human endeavour you care to name. Biology is a big one. “Cancer, Alzheimer’s, heart disease, mental illness – these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade,” said Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei while promoting the company’s recent initial public offering . “I think one day maybe we can cure all disease with the help of AI,” said Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind, last year , adding that this could be “within the next decade or so”. This phenomenon isn’t new: I call it “physicist brain”, after the propensity for physicists to wade into areas outside their expertise and declare simple solutions. More broadly, it is called Nobel disease , after the many Nobel prizewinners who have gone on to make, shall we say, less evidenced-backed claims. In general, there is a tendency to think that if an intelligent person is good at one thing, they are good at many other things that require intelligence. What is different now is that trillion-dollar companies and large swathes of the global economy now depend on this being true of artificial intelligence. Advertisement To be clear, I think we must now admit that AI is better at solving open mathematical problems than any human, and that this has happened faster than anyone ever expected. When I first saw the news in September that the Navier-Stokes problem had been solved by OpenAI , I felt stunned. We had entered a new world. With the announcement of the Riemann hypothesis proof this week, I felt sick and had to go and have a lie-down. These were intellectual Everests I have marvelled at since my teenage years, conquered by a machine far sooner than anyone expected. You may have read my recent piece forecasting the future in 2096 – an early draft had a line, later removed, about three Millennium Prize Problems being solved by AI in the 2030s. We’ve had two this year alone. But maths isn’t biology. Yes, we have seen advances like AlphaFold, Deepmind’s AI that can predict the structure of proteins , but this is biology at its most mathematical, a computational puzzle. True advances in biology and medicine require studying cells, animals and people, all of which can be frustratingly illogical and uncooperative. science.title: The defence tech revolution is changing how we innovate
science.description: Cpl Aaron J Stone/UK Ministry of Defence Only five years ago, defence technology start-ups had little choice but to wait for government funding to build and test their inventions – often in complex, multi-year programmes. No longer, however: Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022 has prompted such a fast, furious response that military innovation timescales have shrunk dramatically. “Ukraine is becoming a real-world lab for military innovation, and it’s innovating at a pace greater than anything that we’ve seen previously,” says Ola Fashade, an air vice-marshal in the Royal Air Force and director of military digitalisation and the rapid AI delivery task force at the UK’s Ministry of Defence (MoD). “Agility and tempo of adaptation is critical. In a contested battlespace, technology that works well on day one, by day eight has become a little muted – and by day twelve it’s probably no longer relevant. And if you don’t adapt over that period, what you have is a very expensive and ineffective bag of steel.” Advertisement That raises the question of how significant this accelerated innovation could become. In September 2026, New Scientist CoLab, sponsored by BAE Systems, brought together leading thinkers and investors from industry, the military and academia to discuss the factors driving this innovation and the lessons that can be transferred to other industries. Staying alive The investment for this step change is coming both from the technology incubators based within military prime contractors – like the Launchpad incubator at BAE Systems – and from a host of venture capital (VC) companies worldwide. “The idea behind Launchpad is to forge an ecosystem that gets technology from defence start-ups into the front line quicker, or into spinouts, before they run out of money and die,” says David Ewing, head of technology commercialisation at BAE Systems. In addition, VC funding is seeing a raft of new multibillion-dollar military tech players, dubbed neoprimes, that complement the work of the primes on bigger-ticket battlespace items. The poster child for the neoprimes, says Samuel Burrell, a partner at the pan-European VC firm Expeditions Fund, is the nascent British air defence start-up Cambridge Aerospace, which reached a valuation of $3.4 billion with little but a convincing tech narrative: “They had no battlefield data, no product – just a compelling team and an idea on paper.” It wasn’t all talk: Cambridge Aerospace has begun delivering its Skyhammer air defence missile for taking out Shahed-type drones and cruise missiles. A solid-rocket-motor-powered ballistic missile interceptor, Starhammer, will ship in 2027. science.title: Seeking Refuge on Resolution Island
science.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Seeking Refuge on Resolution… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search In the late 1800s, wildlife conservationists in New Zealand were recognizing how predators such as stoats , brought to the country to control other nonnative animal populations, were becoming a threat to native birds. Naturalists at the time surmised that some of the nation’s islands could serve as sanctuaries where endemic species could persist, free from the voracious newcomers. Resolution Island, located in the Fiordland region along the rugged southwest edge of New Zealand’s South Island, was one of the first eyed for this purpose. Conservationist Thomas Henry Potts proposed in 1872 that the island could be a place where “wingless species, and birds of feeble powers of flight, might there find a refuge for some of their representatives.” So began an early systematic effort to protect kiwi, kākāpō , and other native birds on Resolution Island, the largest of the approximately 90 islands in Fiordland National Park . This image, acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 on December 12, 2025, shows the island’s setting amid a landscape of steep-sided valleys carved by glaciers and now inundated by the ocean. The uninhabited island rises from sea level to the summit of Mount Clerke at 1,069 meters (3,507 feet). Its diverse habitats and vegetation communities range from bogs and wetlands near the coast to widespread podocarp forests at middle elevations to tussock grasslands in the subalpine and alpine areas. Offshore, the Taumoana (Five Fingers Peninsula) Marine Reserve protects estuarine and wave-exposed rocky reef habitats at the entrance to Dusky Sound, east of Five Fingers Peninsula. Farther into the sound, Pigeon Island was the onetime home of Richard Henry, who was named caretaker of Resolution Island after it was designated a reserve in 1891. In what some have called a “ landmark effort ,” Henry spent years transporting more than 700 birds, mostly kiwi and kākāpō, by rowboat to Resolution and other would-be island sanctuaries nearby. In 1900, however, people began spotting mustelids on Resolution. It turns out the island is within swimming distance for animals such as stoats. Henry was intent on trapping the interlopers but eventually abandoned the project and moved on to caretaking work on another island. The spirit of his efforts lives on, though. A Department of Conservation program started in 2008 aims to control stoat populations and bolster native species on Resolution. science.title: December full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Cold Moon
science.description: null The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon).. According to the late, great astronomer Fred Espenak , the Cold Moon will be just 221,667 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth when it turns full, making it the closest supermoon of 2026! When to see the December full moon The full Cold Supermoon will make for a spectacular sight when it rises over the eastern horizon at sunset on Dec. 23, mere hours before reaching maximum illumination. Remember to use Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker for timings specific to your location. Earth's satellite may appear larger than normal while close to the horizon. This is partly because it is near perigee, when it appears subtly larger in the night sky, but also because of a phenomenon called the moon illusion, which tricks us into perceiving the moon to be bigger than it actually is while in the presence of foreground objects. A yellow full moon rises over Italy. (Image credit: Photo by Lorenzo Di Cola/NurPhoto via Getty Images) The moon may also adopt a striking golden or orange hue around moonrise and moonset. When the moon is low on the horizon, its light travels through more of Earth's atmopshere, scattering shorter, bluer wavelengths of light and allowing longer, redder wavelengths to reach our eyes. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 25, 1970: NASA's 'wingless' M2-F3 'lifting body' aircraft makes its 1st powered flight ahead of supersonic tests
science.description: null On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft. After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights. The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet. NASA's M2-F3 lifting body drops from its carrier plane during a test flight in 1970. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered In the late 1960s and early 1970s, NASA was investigating lifting bodies as an approach to both new aircraft and what future spacecraft, and as its number suggests, the M2-F3 was not the first of its kind. In fact, the M2-F3 was a rebuilt version of its predecessor, the M2-F2 lifting body , after that vehicle crashed in a dry lake bed in California's Mojave Desert during an unpowered test flight. That crash (which appears in the opening of the TV show "The Six-Million-Dollar Man") led to upgrades for a better handling lifting body, NASA said. "When the M2-F2 was rebuilt and redesignated the M2-F3, it was modified with an additional third vertical fin – centered between the tip fins – to improve control characteristics," NASA wrote in an overview . Unpowered glide flights for the M2-F3 began in June 1970, but Dana's flight on Nov. 25 of that year was the first time the vehicle fired up its rocket engine to test its controls under powered flight. One vital upgrade on the vehicle was a set of reaction control thrusters to help maintain its orientation. "A reaction jet control system, similar to thrusters used on orbiting spacecraft, was also installed on the M2-F3 to obtain research data about their effectiveness for vehicle control," NASA wrote . "As the M2-F3’s portion of the lifting body program neared an end, it evaluated a rate command augmentation control system and a side-arm control stick similar to side-arm controllers now used on many modern aircraft." If you want, you can see the M2-F3 vehicle today. NASA donated it to the Smithsonian Institution. It is now hanging at the National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. Want more space history? Many large vessels are now legally required to carry automatic identification systems broadcasting their identity and location at regular intervals. Although this has allowed interactions between animals and fisheries to be studied at scale, there are enormous gaps in coverage. In fact, recent research suggests that three-quarters of industrial fishing vessels don’t use the technology, says Jonathan Rutter at the University of Oxford. This is partly because regulations on the types of vessels that are required to share data vary by country. Large satellite ‘blind spots’ also contribute to the problem, he says, and so does subterfuge for the purpose of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing (IUU). Advertisement Read more Most large fishing boats go untracked as ‘dark vessels’ Rutter says that being caught as bycatch in fishing is one of the greatest risks to seabird populations, but if fishing vessels are only tracked “with conventional methods, such footprints of risk may be strikingly incomplete”. The team analysed audio collected from devices attached to seven northern gannets ( Morus bassanus ) and found that one third of the audio detections couldn’t be matched with vessel tracking data – mostly off the UK coast. Overall, 12 per cent of the vessel detections made by the four critically endangered Balearic shearwaters ( Puffinus mauretanicus ) included in the study couldn’t be matched to public data. science.title: Green light for Starmind: SpaceX gets approval to deploy 1 million AI satellites
science.description: null Earth orbit could get a lot more crowded in the coming years. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) just granted SpaceX approval to deploy one million of its Starmind AI data-center satellites in orbit. "This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said today (Nov. 25) in a statement announcing the approval. AI has become central to SpaceX's business plans and identity over the past year or so. For example, the company has said that it's eyeing a "total addressable market" of $28.5 trillion over the long haul — and nearly $23 trillion of that is in "enterprise AI applications." Starmind is key to those lofty ambitions. SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk believes that the future of AI compute is in space, where energy (from the sun ) is unlimited and there are no land-owning neighbors to lodge NIMBY complaints. SpaceX aims to launch the first of its Starmind satellites in the third quarter of 2027. The spacecraft will fly on the company's fully reusable Starship megarocket, which has deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink satellites on its most recent two test flights . Those 52 spacecraft are the vanguard of another enormous constellation: Musk has said that the next-gen Starlink network will eventually consists of about 100,000 satellites . The planned numbers for Starlink and Starmind are truly mind-boggling. To put them into perspective: Since the dawn of the space age in 1957, humanity has launched a total of just 28,000 satellites, give or take a few hundred. And the biggest constellation ever operated to date, the current iteration of Starlink, consists of about 11,000 spacecraft. These coming buildouts will require an enormous number of launches. Starship can carry a maximum of 60 V3 Starlink satellites per launch, for instance, so it will take about 1,700 liftoffs just to assemble that network (and more to maintain it, as the operational life of each satellite is expected to be about five years). Putting so many satellites into orbit also raises the risks of collisions. SpaceX has proven to be extremely proficient in this regard with its current Starlink satellites, which can detect and avoid potential collisions autonomously. But more evasive maneuvers will be required as space gets more and more crowded. SpaceX isn't the only company that aims to operate data centers in space; Cowboy Space , Starcloud, Blue Origin and Google, among other companies, have voiced similar ambitions. science.title: AI’s stunning progress in maths shows how little we understand it
science.description: MARK SYKES/SPL/Alamy There is a story, possibly apocryphal, that when the mathematician G. H. Hardy was about to undertake a dangerous sea voyage, he sent a postcard to a colleague declaring “I have solved the Riemann hypothesis”. Hardy, a staunch atheist, joked that this would prevent his ship from sinking, as God would never let him claim the credit for such a major result without revealing the details of his proof. Hardy would probably be both astonished and aghast that we now have what seems to be a proof of the Riemann hypothesis , a problem that has vexed mathematicians since the 19th century, but that no one yet understands it. The consensus among mathematicians is that the proof, produced with the aid of AI, will hold, but that it will take much more work to make it comprehensible to humans. However you feel about AI, this is a watershed moment, and one that demonstrates just how little we still understand about the capabilities of the technology. As recently as last month, leading mathematician Terence Tao speculated that AI would eventually solve the Riemann hypothesis, but that it may not happen before 2050. Now, some mathematicians are considering whether their hardest and most infamous remaining problems could be settled within months. In a year that has left mathematicians reeling, this may be the knock-out blow. Advertisement This is a watershed moment, and it shows just how little we understand about AI’s abilities For non-mathematicians, the fall of the Riemann hypothesis is harder to interpret. In the past year, AI has seen incredible advances in both maths and coding, but it is perhaps no coincidence that in these arenas, with nothing more than computer code, answers can swiftly be checked and iterated upon, allowing for rapid improvement. When it comes to other human endeavours though, from art to zoology, such verification is far harder, involving either the messy physical world, or unknowable human taste – or both. Whether this verification gap can be closed may become the biggest question of our age. Answers on a postcard, please. What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental? It has been called the hardest problem in mathematics, and now through a combination of human ingenuity and relentlessness, and the computational power of AI, the Riemann hypothesis may have finally been solved
